methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $800M - $7.6B.

private.name: Joby Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $6.86B

data.narrative:
Archer Aviation is a publicly traded drone and autonomous systems company currently valued at $3.33B, having raised $1.5B+ to date. The valuation is anchored against a peer universe of 4 same-sector comparables spanning Series B through public stages, with a wider reference set including 7 private autonomy companies (Joby Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, Elroy Air, and Aurora Innovation among them).

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach here. The 4-company peer cohort—Zipline ($7.6B, Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B, public), Nuro ($6.0B, Series G), and Elroy Air ($800M, Series B)—yields a median valuation of $6.4B, with a range spanning $800M to $7.6B. This median implies a valuation 92% above Archer's current $3.33B mark.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $5.5B to $7.4B (median $6.4B), suggesting Archer trades at a material discount to peer-median levels. The single-method constraint limits conviction; application of additional techniques (revenue multiple, DCF, or transaction precedent analysis) would strengthen the range. Key uncertainties include stage-appropriate discount factors between public and late-stage private peers, cash runway relative to commercialization timelines, and differentiation in core technology versus the broader autonomy cohort.
